shots.say: These chocolate peanut butter pretzel truffles
have three ingredients,
and each one has a wildly different origin story. Stay with me.
Peanuts.
The Incas were cultivating them in South America
as far back as 1500 BCE,
burying them with their mummies
and grinding them into paste.
The Aztecs used peanut paste as a toothache remedy.
America did not discover peanut butter until 1904
at the St. Louis World's Fair.
3000 years later,
but we got there.
Now on to pretzels.
European monks invented them in the Middle Ages
as rewards for children who learned their prayers.
That iconic three-hole shape was meant to represent the Holy Trinity.
German immigrants brought them
to Pennsylvania in the 1700s
and never looked back.
And chocolate.
Ancient Mesoamerica, Aztec currency,
colonial medicine cabinet staple.
American Heritage Chocolate carries that tradition forward with an authentic recipe
from the 1700s.
The same decade pretzels were settling into Pennsylvania
and peanuts were finding their way across trade routes into North America.
And that is exactly why these three ended up in a truffle together.
A truffle is the perfect format for ingredients this bold and distinct.
Rich chocolate on the outside holding together the salty crunch of pretzel
and the deep, nutty weight of peanut butter.
Three ingredients from three completely different corners of history,
each strong enough to stand on its own, and somehow even better together.
Three centuries of history, one truffle.
Full recipe is linked in our bio. Go make them!
